brief: The long game: 6 compounding habits that separate 20-year careers from 2-year sprints.

slots.subtitle: Six quiet disciplines that transform short sprint ambition into enduring professional mastery and legacy.

slots.body: The world rewards what it cannot replicate. Two hours of uninterrupted focus, sustained across decades, outperforms a decade of scattered hustle.
Great careers are built in years, not quarters. The discipline to delay gratification compounds into authority that no shortcut can manufacture.
Trust accrues slowly and erodes instantly. Invest in alliances before you need them; they become your most appreciating asset over time.
Ten years of repetition stagnates; ten years of feedback loops elevate. Seek the uncomfortable margin where skill is forged, not merely maintained.
Optimize for the decade, not the deadline. Decisions made with a twenty-year horizon align your daily actions with your ultimate legacy.
The final differentiator is simply staying power. Those who endure the boring middle, when others quit, claim the rewards of compound endurance.
Sprint when you must, but build for decades. The quiet ones outlast the loud.
